results.title: Since the US military lost access to Air Base 201 in Agadez—formerly Washington's premier ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissanc
results.description:
Since the US military lost access to Air Base 201 in Agadez—formerly Washington's premier ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance) hub in the region—AFRICOM has indeed suffered a severe degradation in real-time visibility over JNIM and Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS) movements.

Across multiple administrations and high-level Pentagon visits (going back to former Defense Secretary Mark Esper's 2020 visit to Algiers and subsequent AFRICOM Memorandums of Understanding), Washington has quietly urged Algeria to abandon its strict constitutional ban on out-of-area operations (amended in 2020) and project stabilizing power southward.

Algeria's Core Motivation is that Algiers is acting purely out of national interest. The immediate catalyst for the deployment is securing Algerian state energy giant Sonatrach’s oil exploration blocks in northern Niger (specifically the Kafra block) and safeguarding the proposed Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline corridor.

results.description:
That junta took power in a 2023 coup that Algeria condemned at the time. Since then, Niger and its neighbours in Mali and Burkina Faso have pushed out the French and the Americans, formed their own alliance and fought al-Qaeda and ISIL affiliates with whoever would help.

The newest partner is the one next door, and the stake is Europe’s gas.

results.title: Yes. The US has provided extensive counterterrorism support in Africa, including Nigeria and the Sahel. In Nigeria: long-term training, equi
results.description:
Yes. The US has provided extensive counterterrorism support in Africa, including Nigeria and the Sahel.

In Nigeria: long-term training, equipment (e.g. Super Tucanos), intelligence sharing, 2025-2026 joint airstrikes and operations that killed senior ISIS leaders and hundreds of fighters, plus temporary troop deployments for advisory roles.

In the Sahel: Trans-Sahara Counterterrorism Partnership, past bases and ISR from Niger, training, and ongoing intelligence cooperation with partners despite post-coup withdrawals.

results.title: The US has done more overall.
results.description:
The US has done more overall. It provides decades of training, equipment, intelligence, and targeted strikes across Nigeria, Somalia, the Sahel, and beyond—recent joint ops in Nigeria alone killed hundreds of ISIS fighters, senior leaders, and seized major intel caches. 

Russia’s Africa Corps focuses on regime protection in junta states like Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. It has helped repel some attacks but shows limited success reducing jihadist expansion; violence remains high there.
